Discrete-Time Model with KL Divergence for Data Integration

discretekl.Rd

Fits a series of grouped-time (discrete-time) survival models that borrow from an external model through the Kullback–Leibler divergence between the two models' interval hazards, one fit per value of the integration weight eta. It is the discrete-time counterpart of coxkl().

Follow-up is recorded in intervals \(1, \dots, K\): subject \(i\) is at risk in intervals \(1, \dots, t_i\) (interval), and delta = 1 when the event happened in interval \(t_i\). The interval hazard is $$h_k(z) = g^{-1}(\gamma_{sk} + z^\top \beta),$$ with one baseline parameter \(\gamma_{sk}\) per stratum and interval and the link \(g\) set by link.

External information can be supplied either as:

  • the external model's interval hazards for your subjects (hazard), or

  • an external Cox (grouped proportional hazards) model: its coefficients (beta) together with its baseline cumulative-hazard increments over your intervals (baseline).

Usage

discretekl(
  z,
  delta,
  interval,
  stratum = NULL,
  hazard = NULL,
  beta = NULL,
  baseline = NULL,
  etas,
  link = c("cloglog", "logit"),
  n_intervals = NULL,
  tol = 1e-09,
  Mstop = 200,
  message = FALSE
)

Arguments

z

Numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) of covariates, one row per subject. Column names are used to align external coefficients by name.

delta

Event indicator: 1 when the event happened in the subject's last interval at risk, 0 when the subject was censored at the end of it.

interval

Whole numbers \(1, \dots, K\): the last interval each subject was at risk in (the interval of the event when delta = 1).

stratum

Optional strata; each stratum has its own baseline hazard over the intervals.

hazard

Optional \(n \times K\) matrix of external interval hazards: row \(i\), column \(k\) is the external model's probability that subject \(i\) has the event in interval \(k\) given that it reached the interval. If not supplied, beta and baseline must be.

beta

Optional named vector of external Cox coefficients, aligned to colnames(z) by name (covariates the external model does not cover are set to 0; see align_beta()).

baseline

Optional external baseline cumulative-hazard increments over intervals \(1, \dots, K\), \(\Delta\Lambda_0(k) = \Lambda_0(t_k) - \Lambda_0(t_{k-1})\). With beta, the external interval hazard is \(1 - \exp\{-e^{z^\top\beta}\Delta\Lambda_0(k)\}\).

etas

Numeric vector of non-negative integration weights; sorted in ascending order.

link

"cloglog" (complementary log-log: the grouped proportional-hazards model, the default, on the scale of a Cox model's coefficients) or "logit" (proportional odds of the interval hazard).

n_intervals

Number of intervals \(K\); defaults to max(interval).

tol

Convergence tolerance of the Fisher-scoring iterations. Default 1e-9.

Mstop

Maximum number of iterations per fit. Default 200.

message

Logical; if TRUE, prints a progress bar.

Value

An object of class "discretekl":

eta

The sorted integration weights.

beta

Matrix of coefficients, \(p \times\) length(etas), one column per eta.

gamma

Array of baseline parameters \(\gamma_{sk}\), strata \(\times K \times\) length(etas), on the link scale.

likelihood

Log-likelihood of the target data at each eta (larger is better).

linear.predictors

Matrix \(z^\top\beta\), one column per eta.

converged

Whether each fit converged.

link, K, strata_levels

The link, the number of intervals and the strata.

Details

The Kullback–Leibler divergence between the external and target interval hazards turns the objective into a binary cross-entropy on the person-intervals with the observed event indicator \(y_{ik}\) replaced by the soft target $$\frac{y_{ik} + \eta\, \tilde h_{ik}}{1 + \eta},$$ where \(\tilde h_{ik}\) is the external hazard of subject \(i\) in interval \(k\). eta = 0 is the target model alone; as eta grows the fit moves toward the external model. This is the estimator of the DiscreteKL package (Wang et al.), computed by Fisher scoring in C++.

See also

cv.discretekl() to choose eta; discretekl_ridge(), discretekl_enet(); cv.bregsurv() with target_discrete() and release_model().

Examples

data(ExampleData_discrete)
tr <- ExampleData_discrete$train
fit <- discretekl(z = tr$z, delta = tr$status, interval = tr$interval,
                  beta = ExampleData_discrete$beta_external,
                  baseline = ExampleData_discrete$baseline_external,
                  etas = c(0, 1, 10))
#> 1 covariate(s) absent from external 'beta' were set to 0: Z6.
fit$beta
#>             0           1           10
#> Z1  0.5812913  0.64400602  0.681017845
#> Z2 -0.7813239 -0.56373185 -0.474929286
#> Z3  0.9250432  0.68477956  0.595543391
#> Z4 -1.2837399 -0.63875508 -0.310304575
#> Z5  0.1817395  0.29280574  0.362306547
#> Z6 -0.1391096 -0.05318527 -0.008176801
